Every row whose status is not ok leaves the estimate columns blank (n_analytic through p_value). A failed specification stays in the file.

The option this specification used, for each dimension you varied, using the option names from your preregistration exactly. All nine columns are present, in numeric order; those you did not vary are blank throughout.
column5: An option name is its prefix (orig_ or alt_) followed by a short lowercase description with underscores, e.g. orig_exclude_pilot_wave. A bare orig_ or alt_ is not a name

column4: The same, for any paper-specific additions you varied. After d09.
The number of observations the analysis used: not the rows in your dataset, and not the sum of any weights.

The focal estimate, identified by name, on the scale your analysis produces it. For a logistic, Poisson or Cox regression, the log-scale coefficient. Where an option makes the focal estimate multi-valued, the single contrast named in your preregistration.
1 if the estimate is standardized.
The estimate's standard error. For a multi-valued focal estimate, the named contrast's.

The test statistic for the focal estimate. For a multi-valued focal estimate, the joint test of the whole set, which test_stat_type, df1, df2 and p_value then also describe; estimate divided by se does not reproduce it.
The kind of test statistic.
Degrees of freedom, or the numerator degrees of freedom where there are two.
The denominator degrees of freedom, where there are two.
The effect size, such as the odds ratio from a logistic regression. Blank where the estimate is already the effect size.
What effect_size measures.
column5: OR, RR, HR, IRR, d, r, smd, other

column4: The p-value for the focal estimate.
Whether the specification ran and produced the focal estimate.
column5:
ok: ran and produced the focal estimate
nonconvergence: the fitting algorithm did not converge
singular: part of the model could not be estimated (use not_estimable if that part is the focal estimate)
insufficient_n: too few observations remained
degenerate: the model reproduces its data exactly, leaving no residual variation
not_estimable: could not be run, or ran without producing the focal estimate
other: say what in error_message
